title: Hörmander Estimates and the Levi Problem

items.title: Smooth strict plurisubharmonic regularization of a psh exhaustion
items.statement: Under AC and countable choice, a continuous psh exhaustion on a domain Ω⊂ℂⁿ, n≥1, admits a smooth strict psh majorant with an increasing sequence of regular compact strongly pseudoconvex sublevels.

references.title: Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry
references.locator: Ch. I §5.E, Theorem 5.21 (Richberg 1968), printed pp. 43-44: smooth approximation from above of continuous strictly plurisubharmonic functions with a positive Hessian lower bound.

items.proof_strategy: Apply Demailly Richberg Thm. 5.21 to u+|z|²+1 with a strict positive Hessian lower bound, then select regular values by Sard and countable choice.

items.title: Meromorphic functions on an open set in complex Euclidean space
items.statement: A meromorphic function is a compatible local quotient class; a representative with removable omissions is holomorphic on U exactly when it extends holomorphically to U.

references.title: Jiří Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables
references.locator: Ch. 1 §1.2, the paragraph defining meromorphic functions after Exercise 1.2.19 (a function on a dense open subset that is locally a ratio of holomorphic functions), and §4.6, where the same notion is used for the Cousin I problem.

references.title: Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry
references.locator: Ch. I §6.2, the sheaf of germs of meromorphic functions: sections over an open set are meromorphic functions, representable locally as quotients of holomorphic functions, and the pole set is closed with empty interior.

items.proof_strategy: Definition of the standard local-quotient notion of a meromorphic function in several complex variables, its restriction, holomorphy on an open subset, and sums with holomorphic functions. No proof obligation.

items.title: Weighted L² spaces and maximal ∂̄ operators
items.statement: Assume AC, n≥1 and open Ω⊂ℂⁿ. Define weighted coefficient Hilbert spaces, maximal distributional ∂̄ and its between-degree Hilbert adjoint, with declared one-based aliases and empty-domain conventions.

references.title: Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry
references.locator: Ch. VIII §§1 and 3, printed pp. 363-372: unbounded operators, distributional d''-operators, and the warning that the Hilbert adjoint need not coincide with the formal expression on a boundary domain.

references.title: Harold P. Boas, Lecture Notes on Several Complex Variables
references.locator: §3.3.3, printed pp. 81-83: distributional dbar, membership of a form in the domain of the Hilbert adjoint, and the boundary condition.

references.title: Mohammad Jabbari, Several Complex Variables course notes
references.locator: §§4.1.1-4.1.3, PDF pp. 67-84: weighted L2 spaces of forms, maximal closed extension, and the adjoint formula.

items.proof_strategy: The weighted norm is Hilbert because e^{-φ} is positive and locally bounded above and below; multiplication by e^{-φ/2} identifies it with ordinary L². Define the maximal operator by its distributional graph domain and its Hilbert adjoint by the Riesz pairing. Keep that Hilbert adjoint distinct from the formal expression unless a core or boundary argument identifies them.

items.title: The maximal distributional ∂̄ operator is closed and densely defined
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice (AC). Every maximal distributional ∂̄ on weighted L² is densely defined and closed, and its Hilbert adjoint is closed; on compactly supported tests the adjoint has the formal weighted expression.

references.title: Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry
references.locator: Ch. VIII §3, printed pp. 369-372: closed distributional extensions and the boundary-adjoint warning

references.title: Harold P. Boas, Lecture Notes on Several Complex Variables
references.locator: §3.3.3, printed pp. 81-83: the maximal distributional dbar

references.title: Mohammad Jabbari, Several Complex Variables course notes
references.locator: §§4.1.1-4.1.3, PDF pp. 67-84: maximal closed extension and adjoint formula

items.proof_strategy: Compactly supported smooth forms give density. If u_k→u and ∂̄u_k→v in weighted L², local L¹ convergence passes the test-function identity to ∂̄u=v, proving graph closure. The unbounded-operator adjoint theorem gives a closed adjoint. Testing against compactly supported forms identifies only its interior expression: on a boundary domain the adjoint may impose extra boundary conditions.

items.title: Basic Bochner–Kodaira–Morrey estimate on ℂⁿ
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice (AC). For φ∈C²(Ω) psh and compactly supported smooth (0,q)-form u, q≥1, ∥∂̄u∥²φ+∥∂̄*φu∥²φ≥∫ΩΣ_{|J|=q−1}Σ_{j,k}φ_{j\bar k}u_{jJ}\overline{u_{kJ}}e^{-φ}dV.

references.title: Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry
references.locator: Ch. VII §1 (1.2), printed p. 330 (Bochner–Kodaira–Nakano identity); Ch. VIII §4 (4.1)–(4.2), printed pp. 370-371 (general d'' estimate)

references.title: Harold P. Boas, Lecture Notes on Several Complex Variables
references.locator: §3.3.3, printed pp. 81-85: the basic estimate proved by integration by parts, and Exercise 38 for the weighted computation

references.title: Mohammad Jabbari, Several Complex Variables course notes
references.locator: §4.3, Theorem 84 and Lemma 85, PDF pp. 97-98 (weighted L2 estimate for the d-bar problem)

items.proof_strategy: Expand ∂̄ and its formal weighted adjoint in coordinates and integrate mixed derivatives by parts. Compact support removes boundary terms; their commutator is multiplication by φ_{j ar k}. Remaining derivative-square terms are nonnegative. Summing the coefficient identities yields the Levi quadratic form. This is the interior estimate; the separate smooth-boundary lemma records the boundary contribution.

items.title: A coercive Hilbert-complex estimate solves the closed equation
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice (AC). Let $T$ and $S$ be closed densely defined operators with $ST=0$. If $\|T^*v\|^2+\|Sv\|^2\ge C\|v\|^2$ on $\operatorname{Dom}(T^*)\cap\operatorname{Dom}(S)$, then every $f\in\ker S$ equals $Tu$ for some $u$, and the least-norm solution obeys $\|u_0\|\le C^{-1/2}\|f\|$; moreover, if a bounded self-adjoint $A\ge0$ satisfies $\langle Av,v\rangle\le\|T^*v\|^2+\|Sv\|^2$ on that domain and $f=Ag$, then the least-norm solution obeys $\|u_0\|^2\le\langle f,g\rangle$.

references.title: Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry
references.locator: Ch. VIII §1, Theorem 1.2 and proof, printed pp. 364-365 (von Neumann Theorem 1.1 on p. 364); the coercivity hypothesis is (1.3). Ch. VIII §4, Theorem 4.5 and its proof, printed pp. 370-372: the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality with the A-weight and the Hahn-Banach step repeated from Th. 1.2.

references.title: Mohammad Jabbari, Several Complex Variables course notes
references.locator: §4.1.2, Theorem 72 and its proof, PDF pp. 85-87, with the energy estimate (4.4) and the orthogonal-decomposition argument.

references.title: Harold P. Boas, Lecture Notes on Several Complex Variables
references.locator: §3.3.3, printed pp. 81-82: the basic estimate implies existence of a solution of the dbar equation in L2.

items.proof_strategy: Prove the between-Hilbert-space graph complement and adjoint projection directly, then apply the coercive estimate for a minimal solution.

items.title: Weighted Morrey–Kohn estimate with a pseudoconvex boundary term
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice (AC). On a bounded C∞ pseudoconvex D with C² weight φ, smooth (0,q)-forms satisfying the ∂̄-Neumann boundary condition obey the weighted Levi estimate plus a nonnegative boundary Levi-form term; in particular the Hessian controls the sum of the q smallest eigenvalues.

references.title: Harold P. Boas, Lecture Notes on Several Complex Variables
references.locator: §3.3.3, printed pp. 81-85: formulas (3.3)-(3.5), the ∂̄-Neumann boundary condition (3.4), and Exercise 38 for the weighted computation

references.title: Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry
references.locator: Ch. VIII §4 (4.1)-(4.2) and §6 (6.4)-(6.5), printed pp. 370-373: general estimate and smallest-eigenvalue bound

references.title: Friedrich Haslinger, The ∂̄-Neumann Problem and Schrödinger Operators, 2nd edition
references.locator: §4.3, Proposition 4.53 and (4.27) (boundary criterion for dom ∂̄*, unweighted inner product); §5.2, Proposition 5.14 with (5.20) and Lemmas 5.16-5.18, printed pp. 119-124 (graph-norm density of smooth forms with the boundary condition, unweighted inner product)

items.proof_strategy: Transport the weighted adjoint by e^-φ to the unweighted domain; apply the boundary Levi estimate and Haslinger graph-norm density.

items.title: Weighted ∂̄ solvability on a smoothly bounded pseudoconvex domain
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice (AC). For bounded smooth pseudoconvex D and φ∈C²(D̄) strictly psh, every closed f∈L²_{0,q}(D,e^{-φ}) has u∈Dom ∂̄ with ∂̄u=f and ∥u∥²φ≤∫D|f|²/(λ₁+⋯+λ_q)e^{-φ}dV.

references.title: Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry
references.locator: Ch. VIII §4, Theorem 4.5 with its proof and Remark 4.8, printed pp. 370-372 (the A-weighted estimate and the smallest-eigenvalue bound); Ch. VIII §6, Theorem 6.5 with (6.4), printed pp. 377-378

references.title: Harold P. Boas, Lecture Notes on Several Complex Variables
references.locator: §3.3.3, printed pp. 81-85: the basic estimate and the resulting solvability of the ∂̄ equation in L2

references.title: Mohammad Jabbari, Several Complex Variables course notes
references.locator: §4.3, the energy estimate (4.4) and Theorem 72 applied to T=∂̄_{q-1}, S=∂̄_q, PDF pp. 85-87

items.proof_strategy: Apply the boundary estimate to T=∂̄_{q−1}, S=∂̄_q. On ker S, the eigenvalue lower bound is coercive by (λ₁+⋯+λ_q)^{-1}; the abstract Hilbert-complex result supplies u and the explicit norm bound. The adjoint domain is precisely the ∂̄-Neumann boundary condition required by the integration-by-parts estimate.

items.title: Smooth strictly plurisubharmonic exhaustion of a pseudoconvex domain
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice (AC). Every Hartogs pseudoconvex Ω⊂ℂⁿ has a C∞ strictly psh exhaustion with increasing regular-value sublevels that are relatively compact, smoothly bounded and strongly pseudoconvex.

references.title: Harold P. Boas, Lecture Notes on Several Complex Variables
references.locator: §3.2.4, Theorem 19 and its proof, printed pp. 69-70

references.title: Jiří Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables
references.locator: Ch. 2 §2.5, Theorem 2.5.6 and the exhaustion characterization

items.proof_strategy: SC-4 gives a continuous psh exhaustion; regularize it smoothly and strictly by the preceding construction while adding coercive growth. Select regular values tending to infinity by Sard. Properness makes the sublevels relatively compact, and the positive Levi form restricts positively to each complex boundary tangent. This is the exhaustion input for nonsmooth-domain estimates and does not invoke Levi’s equivalence.

items.title: Hörmander weighted L² existence theorem for ∂̄
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice (AC). For pseudoconvex Ω⊂ℂⁿ, φ∈C² with positive Levi eigenvalues λ₁≤⋯≤λₙ, closed f∈L²_{0,q}(Ω,e^{-φ}) with finite ∫Ω|f|²/(λ₁+⋯+λ_q)e^{-φ}dV, q≥1, has u∈L²_{0,q−1} with ∂̄u=f and ∫Ω|u|²e^{-φ}dV≤∫Ω|f|²/(λ₁+⋯+λ_q)e^{-φ}dV. Smooth data admit a smooth solution.

references.title: Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry
references.locator: Ch. VIII §6, Theorem 6.5 with (6.4) and its proof, printed pp. 377-379: the semipositive weight estimate and the L2loc (resp. C-infinity) solvability branch

references.title: Harold P. Boas, Lecture Notes on Several Complex Variables
references.locator: §§3.3.2-3.3.3, printed pp. 79-85: the solution of the dbar equation on smooth pseudoconvex domains by the basic estimate, in the (0,1) case

references.title: Mohammad Jabbari, Several Complex Variables course notes
references.locator: §§4.1-4.3, PDF pp. 67-83: weighted L2 spaces, unbounded operators and the energy estimate (4.4) with Theorem 72

items.proof_strategy: Solve on nested connected components of regular psh sublevels containing a fixed basepoint and exhaust the connected domain by compact polygonal paths.

items.title: Positive-degree Dolbeault vanishing on pseudoconvex domains
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice (AC). For q≥1 on pseudoconvex Ω, every smooth closed (0,q)-form has a smooth primitive; every weighted L² closed class satisfying the Hörmander finite-energy condition is exact in the weighted L² complex.

references.title: Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry
references.locator: Ch. VIII §6, Theorem 6.5 with (6.4), printed pp. 377-379: the weighted L2 existence theorem on a weakly pseudoconvex Kahler manifold and its L2loc (resp. C-infinity) solvability branches

references.title: Mohammad Jabbari, Several Complex Variables course notes
references.locator: §4.3, PDF pp. 79-83: weighted L2 spaces, the energy estimate and the vanishing statement for pseudoconvex domains

references.title: Jiří Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables
references.locator: Ch. 4 §4.6, cohomology and the Cousin-I interface

items.proof_strategy: The finite-energy L² statement is exactly the estimate. For arbitrary smooth closed data, choose a convex increasing function of a strict psh exhaustion whose growth dominates coefficient bounds on successive compact shells; its Hessian remains positive and the weighted energy is finite. Apply the theorem and its interior smooth-data regularity. No unweighted L² claim is made for arbitrary smooth data.

items.title: A strictly pseudoconvex boundary point has a local holomorphic separator
items.statement: At a strongly pseudoconvex boundary point, with declared one-based coordinate aliases, the Levi polynomial gives the local holomorphic separator under the stated tangent positivity.

references.title: Harold P. Boas, Lecture Notes on Several Complex Variables
references.locator: §3.3.2, formula (3.1) and the local construction of the separator $f_p$, printed p. 76; §3.2.4, printed pp. 74-75, strong convexity of regular level sets.

references.title: Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry
references.locator: Ch. VIII §7.C, Levi form of the boundary (7.12)-(7.13) and Exercise 8.12(b),(c), printed pp. 61-62; the local model Re w_n + sum lambda_j |w_j|^2 + o(|w|^2) with lambda_n freely assignable.

items.proof_strategy: Flatten the boundary at p and Taylor-expand a defining function in coordinates with tangent plane Re z_n=0. Positivity of the tangential Levi matrix lets a holomorphic quadratic polynomial cancel pure holomorphic quadratic terms. After shrinking V, its real part on the domain side is bounded below by c(|z′|²+|z_n|); hence it vanishes only at p and supplies the local divisor used in reciprocal correction.

items.title: Positive smooth collars for strictly plurisubharmonic negative sets
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $D\subset\mathbb C^n$, $n\ge1$, be bounded and open, with nonempty boundary. Suppose $U\supset\overline D$ is open, $\rho\in C^\infty(U,\mathbb R)$, $D=\{\rho<0\}$ in $U$, and $\rho$ is strictly plurisubharmonic near $\partial D$. No nonvanishing-gradient condition is imposed.

For every open $O$ with $\overline D\subset O\subset U$, there are finitely many pairwise disjoint bounded domains $G_1,\ldots,G_N$ such that
$$\overline D\subset G:=\bigcup_{i=1}^N G_i,\qquad \overline G\subset O,$$
each $G_i$ has $C^\infty$ strongly pseudoconvex boundary, and each $G_i$ admits a continuous plurisubharmonic exhaustion.

references.title: Harold P. Boas, Lecture Notes on Several Complex Variables
references.locator: §3.3.2, printed pp. 76–77, outside smooth strongly pseudoconvex neighborhoods for the cutoff correction. This item proves the needed neighborhood construction explicitly, including extra zeros and critical boundary points.

items.proof_strategy: direct

items.title: Smooth global defining functions for strongly pseudoconvex boundaries
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $D\subset\mathbb C^n$, $n\ge1$, be a bounded domain with $C^\infty$ boundary, strongly pseudoconvex at every boundary point. Then there are a neighborhood $U$ of $\overline D$ and $\rho\in C^\infty(U,\mathbb R)$ with $D=\{\rho<0\}$ in $U$, $d\rho\ne0$ on $\partial D$, and $\rho$ strictly plurisubharmonic near $\partial D$.

references.title: Mohammad Jabbari, Several Complex Variables course notes
references.locator: §3.6.4, Theorem 64(1), printed p. 74: exponential improvement of a defining function. The smooth globalization from smooth local data is proved explicitly here.

items.proof_strategy: direct

items.title: A smooth psh exhaustion gives Hartogs pseudoconvexity on bounded domains
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb C^n$, $n\ge1$, be a bounded domain with a smooth plurisubharmonic exhaustion $S$. Then $\Omega$ is Hartogs pseudoconvex: $-\log\delta_\Omega$ is plurisubharmonic, where $\delta_\Omega$ is the equal-radius polydisc boundary function.

references.title: Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry
references.locator: Ch. I §7.A, Theorem 7.2(c)→(d), printed p. 54: two-disc continuation using a psh exhaustion. The final norm comparison below uses the library equal-radius polydisc convention, not Euclidean distance.

items.proof_strategy: direct

items.title: A strongly pseudoconvex boundary point admits a holomorphic peak function
items.statement: Assume AC. For a bounded domain with a smooth strictly psh defining function near its boundary, or a bounded smooth strongly pseudoconvex domain, every boundary point has a holomorphic peak function on a neighborhood of the closure.

references.title: Harold P. Boas, Lecture Notes on Several Complex Variables
references.locator: §3.3.2, printed pp. 76-77: the local holomorphic separator from formula (3.1), the cutoff, the smooth correction $v$ with $\partial v=(\partial\chi)/f_p$, the reciprocal correction $g=1/[c+v-(\chi/f_p)]$ and the peak function $e^{-g}$.

references.title: Mohammad Jabbari, Several Complex Variables course notes
references.locator: §3.6.4, Theorem 64(1), PDF pp. 74-75: a bounded strongly Levi pseudoconvex open set admits the strictly plurisubharmonic defining function $\rho=\exp(Cr)-1$ on a neighbourhood of its boundary.

references.title: Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry
references.locator: Ch. I (6.13)(a), printed p. 50, and Ch. VIII (5.1), printed p. 375 (weak pseudoconvexity means a smooth plurisubharmonic exhaustion exists); Ch. VIII §6, Theorem 6.5 with its proof, printed pp. 377-379 (the $C^\infty$ solvability branch on a weakly pseudoconvex Kaehler manifold).

items.proof_strategy: Uniform Levi-polynomial separator, proven positive outer collar and radial cutoff; exact polydisc Hartogs bridge and smooth Hörmander correction; removable corrected quotient and exponential peak. Both original Statement branches retained.

items.title: Oka–Weil approximation on a domain of holomorphy (host-domain lemma)
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice (AC). Let D be a domain of holomorphy, K⊂D compact O(D)-convex, and f holomorphic near K. For every ε>0 there is F∈O(D) with sup_K|F−f|<ε.

references.title: Harold P. Boas, Lecture Notes on Several Complex Variables
references.locator: §3.3.2, Theorem 21 with its complete proof, printed pp. 78-79: the analytic-polyhedron reduction, Oka's graph lift, the cutoff correction, the Maclaurin expansion in the graph variable, and the telescoping exhaustion.

references.title: Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry
references.locator: Ch. I (6.13)(a), printed p. 50, and Ch. VIII (5.1), printed p. 375 (weak pseudoconvexity); Ch. VIII §6, Theorem 6.5 with its proof, printed pp. 377-379 (the $C^\infty$ solvability branch used for the graph correction).

references.title: Jiri Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables
references.locator: Ch. 2 §2.6, Theorem 2.6.2 statement and the Oka-Weil discussion; its reverse Levi direction is expressly omitted there, so the host-domain argument is taken from Boas.

items.proof_strategy: Apply Boas §3.3.2 Theorem 21 directly to a holomorphically convex compact K, with the empty compact case vacuous.

items.title: Levi problem: pseudoconvexity and domains of holomorphy
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice (AC). For a domain Ω⊂ℂⁿ, Hartogs pseudoconvexity is equivalent to being a domain of holomorphy and, by Cartan–Thullen, to O(Ω)-holomorphic convexity.

references.title: Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry
references.locator: Ch. I §7.A, Theorem 7.2(c)⇒(e), printed pp. 54-55; Ch. VIII §9, Theorem 9.11(a) and proof, printed pp. 392-393. The latter uses Skoda's Theorem 9.10 to prove pseudoconvexity implies domain of holomorphy.

items.proof_strategy: Use Demailly Ch. I Thm. 7.2(c)⇒(e) and Ch. VIII Thm. 9.11(a) for proper pseudoconvex domains, then Cartan–Thullen and the whole-space hull argument.

items.title: Behnke–Stein: increasing unions of pseudoconvex domains
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice (AC). For increasing pseudoconvex domains Ω_j⊂ℂⁿ whose union Ω is a domain, Ω is pseudoconvex, including Ω=ℂⁿ under the whole-space convention.

references.title: Jiri Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables
references.locator: Ch. 2 §2.5, the nested-union discussion, and the remark that the union statement needs no Levi theory.

references.title: Harold P. Boas, Lecture Notes on Several Complex Variables
references.locator: §3.2.4, pseudoconvexity conventions and the boundary-distance function.

references.title: Mohammad Jabbari, Several Complex Variables course notes
references.locator: §4.2, statement of the Behnke-Stein theorem for increasing unions.

items.proof_strategy: If Ω=ℂⁿ, apply the whole-space convention directly. Otherwise F=ℂⁿ\Ω is nonempty. For z∈Ω, eventually δ_j(z)=dist∞(z,ℂⁿ\Ω_j)>0; these distances increase and are bounded above by δ_Ω(z). Their limit equals δ_Ω(z): choose nearest points in the nested nonempty closed complements; bounded distances place them in a compact Euclidean ball, and a convergent subsequence lands in their intersection F. For each compact subset of Ω choose J whose open Ω_J contains it. On Ω_J the psh functions −log δ_j decrease to finite −log δ_Ω, so the SC-4 decreasing-limit theorem makes that limit psh. Therefore Ω is Hartogs psc. The empty-complement case is handled separately rather than applying a distance formula to an empty set.

items.title: Oka–Weil approximation on a pseudoconvex domain
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice (AC). If Ω is pseudoconvex, K⊂Ω is compact O(Ω)-convex and f is holomorphic near K, then O(Ω) uniformly approximates f on K.

references.title: Harold P. Boas, Lecture Notes on Several Complex Variables
references.locator: §3.3.2, Theorem 21, printed pp. 78-79: Oka-Weil approximation on a domain of holomorphy, combined with the solution of the Levi problem on printed pp. 79-80.

references.title: Jiri Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables
references.locator: Ch. 2 §2.6, Theorem 2.6.2 and the Oka-Weil discussion: statement and scope cross-check.

items.proof_strategy: Apply the Levi theorem to identify Ω as a domain of holomorphy, then apply the host-domain lemma with D=Ω. The final theorem preserves the host lemma hypotheses and is downstream of Levi; it is not used to prove Levi.

items.title: Locally finite smooth partitions of unity on domains
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice (AC). For a domain Ω⊂ℂⁿ and open cover, a locally finite smooth partition subordinate to a locally finite refinement exists.

references.title: Mohammad Jabbari, Several Complex Variables course notes
references.locator: §4.1.1, compactly supported smooth localization; §4.1.3, partitions of unity used for the dbar problem.

references.title: Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry
references.locator: Ch. VIII §3, chartwise partitions and compactly supported localization; standard exhaustion-by-shells construction.

items.proof_strategy: Use K_j={|z|≤j, dist(z,ℂⁿ\Ω)≥1/j} (omit the distance constraint for Ω=ℂⁿ) as compact exhaustion. Cover each compact shell K_{j+1}\int K_{j−1} by finitely many nested rational balls with doubled closures inside assigned cover members and adjacent shells. Countable Choice selects these finite lists and standard radial bumps. Shell separation makes the family locally finite; normalize by its positive locally finite sum.

items.title: First Cousin problem on a pseudoconvex domain
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice (AC). For pseudoconvex Ω and locally finite Cousin-I data m_i meromorphic on U_i with m_i−m_j holomorphic on overlaps, one global meromorphic function realizes the prescribed principal parts.

references.title: Jiří Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables
references.locator: Ch. 4 §4.6, Lemma 4.6.4 and Theorem 4.6.5 with their proofs, printed pp. 153-154 (smooth solution of Cousin-I data by a partition of unity, closedness and global holomorphy of the correction, and the final meromorphic gluing).

references.title: Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry
references.locator: Ch. VIII §6.2 (sheaf of meromorphic functions, local quotients without global representation) and Ch. VIII §6, Theorems 6.5/6.9 for the smooth ∂̄-solution used through the in-pair corollary cor-dolbeault-vanishing-pseudoconvex-domain.

references.title: Harold P. Boas, Lecture Notes on Several Complex Variables
references.locator: §§3.3.2-3.3.3, the ∂̄-correction and L² solvability used to supply the smooth solution of the (0,1)-equation.

items.proof_strategy: Glue meromorphic representatives on their actual open dense domains after solving the closed overlap dbar datum.

title: Hörmander Estimates and the Levi Problem: Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: Hörmander estimate with a Gaussian weight
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice (AC). On ℂⁿ, φ=|z|² and f=d̄z₁ have solution u= ar z₁ attaining equality in the q=1 estimate: both weighted squared norms equal πⁿ.

references.title: Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry
references.locator: Ch. VIII §6, Theorem 6.5, printed pp. 377-379: the weighted $L^2$ estimate with the Gaussian weight $|z|^2$, whose right-hand side the explicit solution attains; the moment computations are the standard polar-coordinate Gamma integrals.

items.proof_strategy: The Levi Hessian is the identity, ∂̄(d̄z₁)=f, and the coefficientwise Gaussian integral factors into n integrals π. This verifies the constant and normalization.

items.title: Levi form of the unit ball
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice (AC). For ρ(z)=|z|²−1, the unit sphere has Levi form Lρ(ξ)=|ξ|² on complex tangent vectors, so the unit ball is strongly pseudoconvex.

references.title: Harold P. Boas, Lecture Notes on Several Complex Variables
references.locator: §3.2.4, Levi form criterion and the model strongly pseudoconvex domain.

references.title: Jiri Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables
references.locator: Ch. 2 §§2.3–2.5, Levi form of |z|^2 and strong pseudoconvexity.

items.proof_strategy: Differentiate ρ_{j ar k}=δ_{jk}; the gradient is nonzero on the sphere and the restriction is positive on every nonzero complex tangent vector.

items.title: An explicit ∂̄ solution with an L² estimate
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice (AC). On ℂ with φ=2|z|², f= ar z d̄z and u=½ ar z² satisfy ∂̄u=f and ∫|u|²e^{-φ}dA=π/16≤π/8=½∫|f|²e^{-φ}dA.

references.title: Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry
references.locator: Ch. VIII §6, Theorem 6.5, printed pp. 377-379: the weighted $L^2$ solvability estimate that the example instantiates; the moment computations are the standard polar-coordinate Gamma integrals.

items.proof_strategy: Differentiate u and use the sole Levi eigenvalue λ₁=2. The identity ∫ℂ|z|^{2k}e^{-a|z|²}dA=πk!/a^{k+1} gives the displayed values.

items.title: A strictly psh exhaustion of the unit ball
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice (AC). The convex unit ball has smooth strict psh exhaustion ψ(z)=−log(1−|z|²).

references.title: Harold P. Boas, Lecture Notes on Several Complex Variables
references.locator: §3.2.4, plurisubharmonic exhaustions and strictly pseudoconvex examples

references.title: Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry
references.locator: Ch. VIII §5, exhaustion functions on the ball

items.proof_strategy: The function diverges at the sphere. Its Hessian is I/(1−|z|²)+( ar z_jz_k)/(1−|z|²)², positive definite; hence its sublevels are compact in the ball.

items.title: Pseudoconvexity of a Hartogs domain
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice (AC). Ω={(z,w):|w|<e^{−|z|²}} is pseudoconvex with smooth strict psh exhaustion ψ=|z|²+|w|²+[1−e^{2|z|²}|w|²]^{−1}.

references.title: Jiri Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables
references.locator: Ch. 2 §§2.3–2.5, Hartogs domains, psh exhaustions and Example 2.5.4.

references.title: Harold P. Boas, Lecture Notes on Several Complex Variables
references.locator: §3.2.4, exhaustion criterion and strictly pseudoconvex examples.

items.proof_strategy: Set s=e^{2|z|²}|w|²<1. Direct differentiation makes s psh, and t↦(1−t)^{-1} is convex increasing, so its composition is psh. The |z|²+|w|² term makes ψ strict. It diverges as |z|→∞ or s→1, proving exhaustion and psc.

items.title: First Cousin gluing on a pseudoconvex domain
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice (AC). On ℂ, U₁={|z|<2}, U₂={|z|>1}, m₁=1/z and m₂=0 form compatible Cousin-I data; G=1/z realizes the prescribed simple pole.

references.title: Harald P. Boas, Lecture Notes on Several Complex Variables
references.locator: §3.3.2, printed pp. 79-80, where the first Cousin problem on a pseudoconvex domain is solved from the Levi problem; the two-chart data here are the classical explicit instance.

items.proof_strategy: On the overlap annulus m₁−m₂=1/z is holomorphic. The global meromorphic function G=1/z has exactly that principal part at 0 and no others.
